- src/utils/annotation-checker.ts (used by require-req-annotation) - reportMissing() for @req: context.report({ node: nameNode, messageId: 'missingReq', data: { name, functionName: name }, fix: createMissingReqFix(node) (when enabled) }); - src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts - meta.messages.missingReq = "Function '{{functionName}}' is missing a required @req annotation. - src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts - meta.messages: - fileMissing: "Story file '{{path}}' not found" - invalidExtension: "Invalid story file extension for '{{path}}', expected '.story.md'" - invalidPath: "Invalid story path '{{path}}'" - fileAccessError: "Could not validate story file '{{path}}' due to a filesystem error: {{error}}. traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria and listed requirements in Story 007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING are implemented and verified: - Core functionality: Every relevant validation rule (require-story-annotation, require-req-annotation, require-branch-annotation, valid-annotation-format, valid-story-reference, valid-req-reference) defines specific, descriptive meta.messages and uses context.report with structured data for function names, paths, and requirement IDs. - ESLint best practices: Rules use messageIds, meta.messages templates with placeholders, and context.report; suggestions are implemented where appropriate (notably require-story-annotation and branch auto-fixes), matching ESLint conventions. - Integration: The rules integrate with existing validation logic from earlier stories, and are exercised via RuleTester-based unit tests and additional helper-based tests; all pass. - User experience: Messages identify the problem (what is missing/invalid), the subject (function/branch/path/reqId), and remediation (add @story/@req, fix path, correct format). For require-story-annotation, tests explicitly verify suggestion text and that functionName is included in the data payload for downstream tooling. - Error handling: valid-story-reference and its helpers distinguish missing files from filesystem/permission errors and report them via dedicated fileAccessError messages; valid-annotation-format handles invalid regex configurations gracefully with invalidRuleConfiguration diagnostics while still validating annotations. - Error consistency and severity: Message patterns are consistent across rules (shared invalid annotation format pattern; shared missingAnnotation for branches; consistent file/requirement error wording and placeholders) and plugin configs map severity exactly as described (missing annotations & missing references = errors; format issues = warnings), with tests confirming this mapping. Given the concrete rule implementations, extensive targeted tests tied back to this story, and the passing Jest test suite, this story is fully implemented and passes.
